messages.subject: Re: shiny integration with other JS frameworks
parts:
I don't think anyone has tried it, but my suspicion is that it should mostly work. I'm not sure if it will make things easier though, it may make things harder and more confusing.

The main thing is that Shiny needs to be notified before and after you modify the DOM if there's the possibility of Shiny inputs/outputs being inside the parts of the DOM you're changing. Assume that "scope" is a DOM node whose children you're about to mess with (you can even use the document object if you want):

Shiny.unbindAll(scope);
// Make changes to the DOM here
Shiny.bindAll(scope);

Also I can't guarantee that these APIs won't change in the future, they're not (yet) part of the officially supported API. That said, they haven't changed in quite a while.
